articleTitle: On Identifying Anomaly Factor Scores Distribution in Estimating Structural Equation Model Using Bayesian Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: The pattern of correlations between many latent components is tested using Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) analysis with Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA). This encompasses multiple model constructs that are assessed using a few observational indicators. Factor scores are the CFA results, which are “new data” for additional examination. It is vital to assess the factor score distribution before conducting additional analysis. This is due to research indicating that factor scores are typically not unimodal and can be bimodal or multimodal. A non-normal or skewed distribution of factor scores is another possibility. There has never been any research done on the distribution of factor scores. For this reason, the factor score distribution will be examined in this study. Before performing further analysis, the factor score distribution needs to be evaluated. The results of this study show that all factor scores from the 9 latent variables are not normally distributed and tend to be skewed. The p-value of the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test for all latent variables is less than 0.01, indicating a departure from normality. This suggests that there's a possibility that the factor scores' distribution is skewed. Several distributions can satisfy this requirement, including the skew-t distribution, skewed normal distribution, and Epsilon Skew Normal (ESN). However, more investigation is required to find the right distribution, which will improve the accuracy of the parameter estimate results.

articleTitle: Streamlining the Handymen Hiring Process in Ilocos Norte Through Mobile Technologies
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: Unemployment remains a significant issue in the Philippines, with a large percentage of the skilled labor force unable to secure jobs. This study focuses on streamlining the hiring process of handymen in Ilocos Norte through mobile technologies. This research aims to identify the usual hiring process, the challenges in the hiring of handymen, the needed handyman skills needed by potential employers in Ilocos Norte, the necessary functionalities of a mobile application, and the user-acceptance of the mobile application in terms functionality, usability, and performance. This research used a combination of qualitative and quantitative methods. The qualitative methods used thematic analysis to identify the usual hiring process in Ilocos Norte and its challenges while the quantitative method is used in interpreting the user-acceptance test. This research will work closely with the handymen and potential employers to ensure that the mobile application will meets their needs, improving the employment opportunities in the Ilocos Norte.

articleTitle: Smart Agriculture: Enhancing Crop Management through IoT-Based Real-Time Monitoring and Automation
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: Internet of Things plays an important role in agriculture in order to provide an innovative and smart solution to traditional farming. IOT is all about connecting physical devices to the internet and can access from a remote place. So that crop monitoring becomes easy even if the farmer is in a remote place. Due to automation, human efforts are required less. Also the IoT data helps the farmer make decisions about planting, harvesting or fertilizing. This paper explains the system we have implemented for monitoring the agriculture with the help of IoT. The system is developed in order to provide real time information on crop conditions to the farmer. For that, it uses various types of sensors connected to the microcontroller in order to measure parameters like temperature, soil moisture, and water level, and accordingly, it activates actuators like a fan, motor or pump to manage ventilation and irrigation. We have used the GSM module to send the alert to the farmer and the WiFi module is used to send the agriculture data to the cloud platform. So that farmer can monitor the farm or crops remotely. The system is continuously collecting farm data from the sensors. If the crop soil is very dry them system will turn on the water pump. Also, for high temperature, the fan will get activated in order to cool down that area. This feature is mostly used in indoor farming. The farmer can monitor the farm condition in real time with the help of cloud platform. This system is helpful for improving productivity, crop management, and save resources i.e. efficient use of water which prevents water wastage.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Transformer Models for Molecular Property Prediction: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: Transformer models, originally successful in natural language processing, are now being applied to chemical and biological studies, excelling in areas such as molecular property prediction, material science, and drug discovery. BERT, a Transformer-based model, has become foundational in cheminformatics, particularly for QSAR (Quantitative Structure-Activity Relationship) modeling and ADMET (Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, and Toxicity) evaluations in drug discovery. However, achieving higher accuracy often requires designing more complex models, which can compromise their interpretability. This posing a challenge for researchers who need to understand the reasoning behind the predictions. The trade-off between accuracy and interpretability presents a critical challenge in applying black box models to real-world problems in cheminformatics. This work compares Transformer-based models with traditional machine learning and deep learning approaches, focusing on both interpretability and performance. The goal is to highlight the strengths and limitations of each method, offering insights into their optimal use in drug discovery and material science.

articleTitle: PCA-SVM for Effective Land Cover Mapping in Bogor Area
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: This paper discusses the mapping of land cover in the Bogor area and classify each pixels from the Landsat satellite images as non-impervious, partial green, or impervious area. The Bogor region has important roles as a water catchment area for the surrounding cities. Lately, the area has experienced urbanization, including the increases in population. This phe-nomenon, in turn, increases the area of impervious surface. The mapping aims to provide mapping information using the PCA-SVM method from 6 spectral channels of Landsat satellite. From the experiments, the PCA-SVM with 2 principal components using Gaussian kernel and regularization parameter <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex> = 100 has the best performance. The evaluation using visual comparison of the mapping with Google Earth Pro is also conducted with satisfactory result.

articleTitle: Detecting Anomalies in Temperature Sensors for Fault Diagnosis in Aviation Meteorology
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: This study focuses on anomaly detection in univari- ate time-series data for fault diagnosis in temperature sensors in aviation meteorology. The algorithms used in this research include Isolation Forest, One-Class SVM, One-Class SVM with Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD), Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) with Autoencoder, Robust Covariance Estimation, and Local Outlier Factor. The analysis was conducted on temperature sensor data from the Automated Weather Observation System (AWOS) at the Juanda Meteorological Station in Sidoarjo. Among the various algorithms tested, the aim was to find a suitable algorithm for anomaly detection for sensor fault diagnosis. The test results showed that the RNN with Autoencoder algorithm was the most suitable because it had the lowest false positive rate. However, it is possible to use other algorithms such as Isolation Forest, One-Class SVM and Robust Covariance Estimation. Because it has a significant difference, namely for the number of anomaly points detected. Damage to the temperature sensor can be detected by the number of anomalies in the data. For recommendations on the anomaly detection process, it is best to use one-period data.

articleTitle: Development of Contactless Entry System with Facemask Detection using Tensor Flow (Api) Application Program Interface
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: This study aimed to design a kiosk-based contactless entry system to minimize manual form completion and trace potential COVID-19 carriers at the Mariano Marcos State University, College of Engineering. The system sought to enhance convenience for students entering the college by incorporating features such as facemask detection, RFID scanning, QR code scanning, and temperature scanning. Facemask detection and temperature sensors were used to identify possible COVID-19 carriers, while RFID and QR codes were employed for contact tracing by collecting user data. A portable, slim design was chosen to ensure ease of deployment. Additionally, a web-based system was developed where students and guests could access their accounts, register, and generate QR codes for seamless entry. To evaluate the effectiveness of the system, functionality tests were conducted on all its features. Researchers also gathered feedback from students to better understand any limitations of the system. The evaluation results were exceptional, showing near-perfect scores across all areas of functionality, convenience, and accuracy. This positive outcome demonstrated that the system significantly streamlined the entry process while maintaining strict health protocols, thereby reducing potential virus transmission. Based on the collected data, the study concluded that the developed kiosk-based contactless entry system was highly effective and successful in achieving its goals of enhancing safety and efficiency for students and visitors at the College of Engineering.

articleTitle: Enhancing Railway Safety with an IoT Based System for Real Time Fault Detection and Crack Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: Safety of railway is the major problem worldwide. It has problems like cracks or any fault in the railway tracks. These problems can cause severe accidents if it is not detected regularly and early. In traditional fault finding and crack detecting method, the manual method is involved which is very slow and consist of many errors. By considering all these challenges and issues in track detection method, we have implemented an advanced IoT based railway crack and fault-finding system. It uses advanced sensors, microcontroller, GPS and GSM module which can detect and report faults of the railway track. The system uses real time mechanism. The system is implemented and tested on a prototype railway track to detect crack or any fault. The internet of things technology added modern and accurate fault-finding feature in the system. The IoT plays an important role in implementing advance technologies, as it uses sensors and advance microcontroller. The accuracy rate of fault and crack detection is around 97%, which is for 2 mm crack. Along with this GPS module accurately track fault location. GSM module successfully send the alert message quickly after detecting the fault in the track. Hence the response time is very less and accurate. This system is implemented in order to ensure safety for the railway track and prevent the accidents. Hence the system is useful for improving overall transport safety.

articleTitle: OpenAI ChatGPT-4 and Google Bard: Proposed Guidelines Based on the Analysis and Educators' Perspectives on the Use of Generative AI Contents Trends
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: This study presents a simple analysis of OpenAI's ChatGPT-4 and Google's Bard, focusing on their similarity indexed, analysis of the content, and the perspectives of educators regarding their application in educational settings. The test was run in the first month 2024 and the research utilized a mixed-methods approach. The research evaluates the similarities and differences between these two leading AI language models. The study assesses similarity indexed and accuracy. Additionally, it gathers insights from educators who are PSU Open University Systems Graduate Students via surveys, exploring their views on the benefits, and challenges of integrating these AI tools in education. The findings reveal distinct strengths and limitations of each model, with ChatGPT-4 excelling in creative content generation and Bard in providing data-backed information. This paper contributes to a deeper understanding of AI's role in education, highlighting the need for balanced and ethically informed AI integration in teaching and learning processes. The paper also suggest a general guidelines in the use of Generative AI.

articleTitle: Smart Energy Management System Using IoT for Real-Time Monitoring and Theft Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: The internet of things technology has developed almost all the sectors including energy management. In traditional energy management system meters are used to recording the number of units and electricity used but they are unable to provide the real time information or updates or any theft of electricity. By focusing this problem, we have developed a system which is able to overcome all the problems in traditional electric management system. It monitors the energy usage and real time theft detection of electricity as it cost lot of money. In our system we have used a current sensor which continuously checks the electricity flow. The microcontroller measures the actual energy usage as well as expected values. It compares both the values. If a big difference found, then it could mean the theft of electricity. So, the GSM module is used to send the alert to the user hence they can take required action. The Wi-Fi module sends the data over the cloud for data analytics. Also, user can see the real time data from the cloud platform. Hence user can track the energy usage and get timely alerts so that user can be aware of energy consumption or energy theft. The system is developed by setting up hardware parts as well as integration with software. The system can be operated or monitored from remote place, as Wi-Fi module connects the system with the internet. System can detect the unusual activities like theft of electricity by analyzing the data. Using the IoT technology for energy management, it can become cost effective as well as smart solution of energy management to avoid any theft. Hence it can overcome the loss.

articleTitle: Comparison of Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, and Amazon Web Services for High-Performance Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)

authors.preferredName: I Gusti Lanang Agung Oka Cahyadi Pradipta

abstract: This study investigates computing-optimized instances from Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, and Amazon Web Services (AWS). Each platform is rigorously evaluated using established high-performance computing (HPC) benchmarks, including HPCC and HPCG, to assess their computational efficiency comprehensively. These benchmarks aim to demonstrate that the optimal cloud solution is application-specific, varying based on workload characteristics. This study offers insights into optimizing cloud resource allocation and management strategies through a comprehensive analysis. The findings are expected to guide organizations in achieving optimal high-performance computing configurations within cloud environments for more efficient computational resources and big data analytics.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of CNN Models for Multiclass Detection on Colon Disease
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: Gastrointestinal diseases are significant health concerns that mostly affect the digestive and biliary tracts. These can only be observed internally through endoscopy, or a modern approach named Wireless Capsule Endoscopy. Though the approach has proven to work, the process relies heavily on medical experts, which is prone to error when given a considerably large load. The use of deep learning in detecting diseases with images has been proven to work in various cases and can be implemented for gastrointestinal diseases. This study compared four deep learning models based on Convolutional Neural Network architectures consisting of the VGG16, ResNet152V2, InceptionV3, and Xception for classifying colon disease images. The experiment showed that the ResNet152V2 performed the best, compared to the other three with a testing accuracy score of 0.9837. On the other hand, the VGG16 had the lowest performance with around accuracy score of 0.89 while the Xception and InceptionV3models yielded similar accuracy scores of 0.9587 and 0.9549, respectively. The results highlight the effectiveness of ResNet152V2 in handling the complexity of colon disease detection

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Fruit and Vegetable Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: In recent times, suppliers in the agricultural sector are under increasing pressure to enhance efficiency in sorting and categorizing fruits and vegetables. Ensuring accurate and efficient detection is crucial for optimizing supply chain operations. This study presents the development of an embedded system using deep learning techniques to address these challenges. Specifically, a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model is implemented on a Raspberry Pi 5, designed to improve the accuracy of fruit and vegetable identification for suppliers. The system integrates image capture and real-time detection capabilities, streamlining the sorting process. The dataset, which includes images of various produce, undergoes preprocessing steps such as grayscale conversion and feature scaling. A train-test split is employed, with 60% of the data allocated for training, 20% for validation, and 20% for testing. The CNN model is trained and evaluated, demonstrating high classification accuracy.

articleTitle: Unlocking Soundscapes: Harnessing Machine Learning for Sound Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: The concept of Smart Cities has been implemented in several major areas to improve the lives of citizens. One of the technologies used is sound classification, which monitors and identifies levels of urban noise. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have proven to be an effective method for sound classification because they can recognize complex patterns in audio data. Various architectures of Convolutional Neural Networks, such as ResNet, DenseNet, and others, exist for this purpose. This research aims to identify the CNN architecture that performs best in urban sound classification. The methodology involves training and testing existing CNN architecture and evaluating them based on several parameters, including the number of parameters, memory usage, convergence speed, and training time. Experimental results show that the performance of the ResNet family tends to degrade when the network depth increases. The best performance was achieved by the Resnet-18 architecture, with accuracy, precision, recall and F1-Score values of 91.5%, 92.2%, 91.2%, 91.6%. On the other hand, the use of complex features from various scales causes the DenseNet and GoogleNet architectures to be unableto achieve the best performance.

articleTitle: Empowering Education Through Transformative Role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Teaching and Learning: Educators' Perspective and Research Trends
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: This research study explores the transformative role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in education. Utilizing a mixed-methods approach, the study combines qualitative data collection techniques and document analysis to determine AI integration in educational settings as perceived by the Open University Systems graduate students who are teachers by profession. Through semi-structured interviews with educators, the study determines the advantages of AI technologies in providing tailored support, enhancing engagement, and improving academic performance. The study also determines the advancement of the increasing number of AI in Education research through a short bibliographic analysis from Scopus database. Recommendations are provided to address these challenges and promote ethical AI practices in the educational landscape. While there is a visible importance of AI in Education, most respondents are concerned about the ethical consideration, and it is recommended to create a policy to be included in the Open University Systems Manual of Operations (OUSOM). Also, while this research aims to contribute to a understanding of AI's transformative potential in education, the findings also see the importance of personalization, efficient assessment, and interactive learning environments.

articleTitle: Object detection of Train Line Equipment using SSD and YOLOv7
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: In modern society, the early detection of damage to train line equipment and regular inspections were essential for ensuring the safe operation of trains. Traditionally, inspections of train line equipment were conducted manually at night. However, this method posed issues such as the need for significant labor and limited mobility. To address these problems, efforts were made to improve mobility by installing cameras on the roofs of test vehicles. However, the analysis of the images captured by these cameras was still conducted manually. In recent years, the use of drones, high-resolution cameras, and AI for inspections had been explored. This paper reported on a preliminary study concerning damage detection of train line equipment using deep learning and its application to autonomous drones. In this study, two models were used for object detection of train line equipment. The target equipment in this study included three components: hanger, connector, and insulator. The dataset contained a total of 2,400 images, with 800 images each for the hanger, connector, and insulator. To evaluate the training progress of the models, the mean Average Precision (mAP) was used for both the training and test datasets. The training was conducted on a Windows PC with CUDA support. The object detection models used were the Single Shot multibox Detector (SSD) and You Only Look Once (YOLOv7). After simulations, the following results were obtained. For the training data, the SSD model achieved an mAP of 73.51%, while the YOLOv7 model achieved an mAP of 97.5%. For the test data, the SSD model achieved an mAP of 53.74%, while the YOLOv7 model achieved an mAP of 76.30%.

articleTitle: Digital Transformation in Higher Education: A Bibliometric Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: Digital transformation (DT) has become a key initiative for organizations, improving resilience and efficiency. The higher education (HE) sector has notably benefited from these advancements. Understanding the current research on digital transformation in higher education (DTHE) is essential for tracking its development as a research field. This study uses bibliometric analysis, drawing on documents from the Scopus database, to review peer-reviewed journals on DTHE published between 2015 and 2023. The analysis focuses on key bibliometric indicators, including authorship, publications, and citations, while also visualizing research trends, co-authorship networks, keyword occurrences, and influential researchers in DTHE. Findings reveal a gradual increase in DTHE publications, with the most prolific authors producing seven articles. Spain, Germany, the United States, and Russia are leading contributors, with Spain, Germany, Norway, and Indonesia showing strong collaborative research efforts. The field has accumulated 2,915 citations, while the most influential institution published only eight articles. This study offers a detailed overview of DTHE research and suggests future directions for both researchers and practitioners in the field.

articleTitle: Optimizing Class Scheduling for the University of Northern Philippines Using Greedy Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: Manual class scheduling at the University of Northern Philippines (UNP) is characterized by inefficiencies, frequent conflicts, and delays, negatively impacting faculty and students. This research explores the development of an automated class scheduling system utilizing the greedy algorithm to address these challenges. The developed system used Agile Methodology to ensure the iterative progress and adaptability, that will allow for ongoing refinements based on the user feedback. The study evaluates current scheduling practices, identifies the appropriate technologies for automation, and designs a web-based application to minimize conflicts and optimize resource allocation. The system uses a greedy algorithm to make locally optimal decisions for globally efficient scheduling. The proposed solution will enhance scheduling accuracy, reduce manual effort, and improve operational efficiency meeting user needs. The proposed system will also manage the conflicts of schedules of the different inputs by its conflict detection and resolution functionality. The research highlights the potential benefits of automated systems in educational settings and offers recommendations for successful implementation.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Navigation System for Train Line Equipment Inspection Using Drones
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: Early damage detection and regular train overhead line equipment inspection are essential for safe and reliable train operation. Traditionally, these inspections have been conducted directly by power line engineers at night. However, such methods face challenges like a shrinking workforce and limited mobility. Attempts have been made to enhance mobility by installing cameras on test vehicles, yet the analysis of captured images still requires manual intervention. With the advancement of drones, high-resolution cameras, and deep learning technology, AI-based inspections using drones have become a promising solution. This study aims to develop an AI-based drone navigation system for automated inspection of train overhead line equipment, focusing on improving inspection efficiency and accuracy through model training for future drone deployment. In this study, a simulator was employed to generate images of overhead line facilities, and a machine learning model was trained using these images, based on the concepts of Dronet and FlowDronet from previous studies. The model's performance was evaluated using varying numbers of training images. A test dataset was created from images captured by a drone in flight and processed with optical flow techniques. The results revealed that the model trained with 22000 images achieved the highest performance, with an Average accuracy of 87.90%, a Collision Recall of 89.60%, and a Non-Collision Recall of 85.99%. These findings underscore the importance of larger datasets in enhancing model generalization capabilities and demonstrate the effectiveness of utilizing drones and AI for automated inspection of train overhead line equipment.

articleTitle: Feature Extraction for Facial Skin Type Classification Using Photo Images
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: Understanding skin type is the first step in selecting skincare or makeup products. This is done to choose appropriate skincare products, address specific skin issues, or minimize mistakes in selecting skincare treatments. Therefore, research needs to be conducted to develop a model aimed at classifying facial skin types using photographic images. In previous studies, image classification modeling using the CNN method has been shown to produce better results compared to other models. The modeling uses the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) method by exploring its architectures, namely MobileNetV1, MobileNetV2, and MobileNetV3Large, to find the best architecture. A total of 588 images were successfully collected and used in the research, obtained directly and labeled by a doctor based on skin type. From this data, 80% was used for training and 20% for testing. The modeling process began with image data preprocessing, followed by training, testing, and model evaluation. The comparison of modeling results for each architecture showed that the MobileNetV3Large architecture was quite suitable for classifying facial skin types, with a validation accuracy of 45% and a training accuracy of 49%. After evaluation, it was concluded that the image data needed improvement. Based on a re-modeling with improved images using the MobileNetV3Large architecture, the results showed a validation accuracy of 48% and a training accuracy of 51%, indicating an improvement after the image data was refined.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Performance of 5G Enabled Embedded Sensor Networks: Proof-of-Function
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: The fifth generation of cellular technology, known as 5G, marks a substantial evolution beyond the fourth generation (4G) standards, offering advancements in speed, connectivity, and overall performance. This research addresses the subject of evaluating 5G's practical implementation in sensor networks, which is fundamental for understanding the real-world applicability. The study explores the practical implementation of a 5G embedded sensor network, focusing on understanding how the network operates, assessing its performance, and identifying potential limitations using hardware components such as Raspberry Pi 3 and DHT22 sensors. The study reveals that while 5G technology offers improvements, different accessibility to the frequency bands across various locations can influence network performance. This variability may affect the widespread deployment and acceptance of 5G sensor networks. Despite these challenges, the research demonstrates that 5G technology can maintain low latency and stable throughput, demonstrating the potential to improve real-time applications and provide reliable data transfer in different environments.

articleTitle: DCK-Means Plus: A Clustering Model for APC's Document Management
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: Organizing and categorizing educational materials play a vital role in creating effective learning environments. At Asia Pacific College, there is a clear need for efficient management and retrieval of Project- Based Learning (PBL) documents. These documents are the final project documentation submitted after the final evaluation from the board of panelist, adviser and teacher. Document clustering is a practical approach to streamline information access, aiming to uncover natural groupings within sets of patterns or documents. This study focuses on employing the widely used K- means algorithm as a foundational element in developing a practical and effective document management tailored for Asia Pacific College (APC). By exploring the principles of document clustering, we aim to enhance document organization, accessibility, and overall management within the academic context. The DCK-Means Plus holds promise for optimizing the handling of extensive document repositories, providing a systematic approach to document management within the unique framework of Asia Pacific College.

articleTitle: Leveraging Hybrid Semantic Ontology-based Model for Library Book Recommendation System
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: This paper presents a study on leveraging the Hybrid Semantic Ontology-based (HSO) model for the library book recommendation system (RS). HSO consists of Collaborative Filtering (CF), Content-based (CB), and Hybrid (HB) modules. HSO can also optionally add a clustering process prior to the CB module to improve its recommendation quality. Despite the promising results of current HSO methods for library book RS, the prospect of further exploitation is still possible. The CF module of HSO implements a matrix factorization, and its choice of algorithm can be different, e.g., Non- Negative Matrix Factorization (NMF) or Singular Value Decomposition (SVD). Meanwhile, the clustering process implements a categorical data clustering technique, and its selected technique can also diverge, e.g., Set-Valued k-Modes (SV-k-Modes) or Density Rough k-Modes (DRk-M). We propose to improve the recommendation quality of library book RS by implementing NMF -based DCG Optimization for Collaborative Ranking (DO-NMF) matrix factorization algorithm and Modified Fuzzy k- Partition (MFkP) clustering technique. Experiment results using the UTM Library Dataset confirm that employing the clustering technique can always improve the HSO model's performance for library book RS. The average performance increase percentage from Top-1 to Top-20 is 60.57%. Meanwhile, both of our proposed methods surpass the performance of all benchmarking methods. The results show that DO-NMF is a superior matrix factorization algorithm to NMF and SVD. Furthermore, MFkP is a better categorical data clustering technique than SV -k-Modes and DRk-M.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Influence of Social Media Marketing on Purchase Intention with Customer Engagement in Industrial Automotive Sales: Case Study: CV Sri Mobilindo Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: The growth of technology and internet users in Indonesia has significantly impacted marketing strategies, with digital marketing, particularly social media, emerging as the most effective tool. Social media's simplicity and connectivity enhance customer interaction, leading to stronger customer relationships and increased purchase propensity. Businesses utilizing digital marketing tools can quickly offer goods and services, create strong client relationships, reduce costs, and potentially improve sales volume. This research aims to explore marketing literature from a Social Cognitive Theory (SCT) perspective, providing theoretical and empirical directions for future research, and offering a clear understanding of SCT in marketing. Emphasizing the importance of analyzing consumer needs and behavior, the study investigates social media marketing, platform credibility, content quality, source credibility, consumer engagement, and purchase intention within CV Sri Mobilindo Motor, an automotive manufacturer. The study seeks to optimize research outcomes applicable for businesses’ long-term objectives and to identify relevant implications and theoretical confirmations between the studied factors. An online questionnaire was distributed to 400 respondents, who are prospective customers of CV Sri Mobilindo Motor and have interacted with content or viewed advertisements on various social media platforms. The responses were analyzed using Smart PLS 3, applying the Structural Equation Modeling-Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) approach to determine the influence and correlation of each variable. The primary goal is to ascertain the impact of digital marketing, particularly social media, on customer engagement and how this engagement affects purchase intention. By understanding these dynamics, businesses can better tailor their digital marketing strategies to enhance customer interaction and drive sales. This study contributes to the theoretical and practical understanding of digital marketing's role in fostering customer engagement and influencing purchase behavior, providing valuable insights for optimizing marketing strategies in the digital era.

articleTitle: Comparing K-Means and DBSCAN Algorithms for Clustering Poverty Levels in Papua Islands
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: Poverty has become one of the main challenges in Indonesia, especially in the eastern regions. According to data from the Central Bureau of Statistics (BPS), Papua Island currently ranks as the poorest province. As of 2018, the poverty rate in Papua was 27.6%, and as of March 2023, it was 26.03%. The government has made various efforts to address the issue of poverty in Papua, one of which is providing financial assistance in the form of BLT (Direct Cash Assistance). However, to achieve sustainable development, more effective and targeted strategies are needed. The government's efforts to address poverty in Papua must be supported by accurate and efficient data analysis. This study involves clustering data on impoverished populations from 42 districts/cities in Papua and West Papua, obtained from the Central Bureau of Statistics (BPS) website in 2023. The study aims to compare the clustering results using the K-Means and DBSCAN algorithms. The performance of these algorithms is determined by the highest Silhouette Index (SI) value. After the data underwent a standardization process, the clustering results using the K-Means algorithm achieved the best SI value of 0.6359 with K=4. Meanwhile, the clustering results using the DBSCAN algorithm achieved the best SI value of 0.3678 with eps 1.8 and MinPts 8. The SI value of the K-Means algorithm is higher than that of the DBSCAN algorithm, indicating that clustering using the K-Means algorithm is superior to DBSCAN.

articleTitle: PeriksAksara: Web-based Indonesian Spelling and Punctuation Correction Using Jaro-Winkler Distance Algorithm Based on KBBI
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: Some of the common issues that affect writing include, but not limited to - spelling errors whereby the writer may miss a certain word because of his/her negligence. This is because it is difficult for a person to observe all correct spelling rules according to the Kamus Besar Bahasa Indonesia (KBBI) also there is also a factor of speed and the movement of fingers while typing. The Jaro-winkler distance method can be used as a solution because it deals with the comparison of two small character strings which can be used to compare the given word that was misspelled with the words in the dictionary which were spelled correctly. It makes the suggestions or auto-completion more accurate and precise by giving more importance on match found at the prefix level. Experiments performed at this stage revealed that using Jaro-Winkler distance enhance the identification of spelling mistakes and generation of correct word suggestion. This result shows that the performance of this method is highly dependent on the quality of the corpus for detection and the quality of the corpus for the prediction of corrections. It means, the higher the quality of the corpus or dictionary used to generate the model, the better will be the predictions for correcting the words in the text.

articleTitle: Hybrid Cooperative Crayfish and Mountain Gazelle Algorithm for Global Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: The crayfish optimization algorithm (COA) and mountain gazelle optimization algorithm (MGO) have emerged as two powerful metaheuristics for global optimization. It has been shown that these two metaheuristics outperform conventional metaheuristics and are capable of finding near-optimal solutions for most of the benchmark functions. However, in certain benchmark functions, COA and MGO do not perform better than the conventional metaheuristics. To this end, a new Hybrid Cooperative COA-MGO algorithm (HCCMGA) is proposed. In the proposed HCCMGA algorithm, the solution vector is split into two solution subvectors of smaller dimensions, one optimized by COA and the other by MGO. The fitness of each search agent in COA and MGA is evaluated in a cooperative manner, whereby the solution subvector in COA is combined with the best solution subvector from MGO and vice versa. The proposed HCCMGA is evaluated using 13 benchmark functions and is compared with several state-of-the-art metaheuristics. Results show that the proposed HCCMGA outperforms state-of-the-arts optimization algorithms in solution quality, search stability and convergence speed, as the HCCMGA achieves solutions closest to the optimum in eight out of the 13 benchmark functions with low standard deviations and less numbers of iterations.

articleTitle: Investigating Trust Determinants in E-commerce Through User Experience and Delivery Satisfaction
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: E-commerce in Indonesia is growing very rapidly. One of the important things in e-commerce business is customer trust. Many things can disrupt customer trust, such as fraud, goods that do not match, long delivery times. Therefore, it is important to learn how customer trust can be formed. This study aims to study the influence of user experience and delivery satisfaction on shopping experience and how trust affects e- commerce platforms. Data were obtained from consumer surveys from e-commerce which were then analyzed using structural equation modeling PLS. This study focuses on studying the relationship between key contracts. The results show that UX has an important role in strengthening customer trust in e-commerce platforms by improving shopping experience. It turns out that delivery satisfaction also has a positive influence on customer trust, although the direct influence on shopping experience is minimal. The results of the study show that shopping experience has an important role in increasing customer trust in e-commerce as a whole. Shopping experience acts as an important mediator.

articleTitle: Unlocking Textual Relationships: Deep Learning for Recognizing Entailment
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: In the field of Natural Language Processing (NLP), understanding implicit meanings in texts is a complex and significant task. This study delves into the use of deep learning models to address these challenges, specifically by focusing on the implementation and evaluation of RoBERTa models. The research compares the performance of RoBERTa with other variations of BERT such as DistilBERT and DeBERTa using evaluation metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, BLEU score and Cohen's Kappa. Findings revealed that RoBERTa outperformed other models achieving an accuracy rate of 88.05%, a precision level of 88.02 %, recall rate at 88.01 % and F1-score score of 88.01 %. Furthermore, with BLEU score of 0.783 and Cohen's Kappa at 0.778, RoBERTa demonstrates its ability to make predictions that are in line with expert annotations and reflect human judgments. This research highlights the potential for advanced BERT models to improve the accuracy and reliability of textual implication identification thus contributing towards more sophisticated and adaptable NLP applications.

articleTitle: Hybrid Agile Model, the Synergy of Waterfall Model and Scrum in a Software Project
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: Hybrid agile is one of the recent software engineering process model used by a software engineering team in a software development project. A hybrid agile model is used by software engineering team to meet the requirements of a software project. However, what does the hybrid agile model used by a software engineering team look like? A qualitative study was conducted to answer this question, and a series of interviews were chosen as a data collection instrument. The interview participants are practitioners involved in software projects using hybrid agile. The recorded interviews are transcribed and analysed using thematic analysis. The finding shows that the software engineering team uses the Waterfall model in the planning, design, deployment and maintenance phases, while scrum in the development and testing phases. The results have led to the hybrid agile model presented in this study, which leverages the strengths of each model to ensure the completion of a software project. Future iterations of this study will assess a project's software quality, comparing the proposed model with plan-driven and scrum.

articleTitle: Improving the Point-of-Sale Operations of the Mariano Marcos State University Through the Integration of Portable Self-Service Kiosk
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: This paper presents the development and implementation of a portable self-service kiosk system at Mariano Marcos State University, designed to enhance the point-of-sale experience in campus canteens. Long wait times during checkout have been identified as a significant issue affecting customer satisfaction and operational efficiency. The proposed system leverages barcode scanning and QR code technology to streamline the ordering and payment process, thereby reducing congestion and wait times. Employing a mixed-methods research design, the study involved qualitative interviews with cashiers and consumers to identify challenges and requirements, followed by quantitative analysis of user acceptance testing results. The agile development methodology was utilized to design, test, and deploy the system, ensuring alignment with user needs throughout the development process. The system incorporates features such as product filtering, canteen selection, notification systems, and consumption pattern-based recommendations. Preliminary results indicate strong user acceptance and satisfaction across four key categories: functionality, usability, efficiency, and portability. The overall grand mean of 4.89 out of 5 in user acceptance testing underscores the system's effectiveness in addressing the identified issues. This innovation not only improves the campus dining experience but also provides valuable data for ongoing service improvements, representing a significant step towards modernizing campus food services at Mariano Marcos State University.

articleTitle: Analysis of Student Trust in the Credibility of Deepfake Video Information on Social Media
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: The development of video technology has made it easier for many people to create videos. One of them is deepfake, where the distribution of deepfake videos is increasing. Students are regarded as an educated group and a generation that frequently uses social media. Therefore, the purpose of this study is to determine whether students easily believe or find it difficult to believe the credibility of deepfake video information that spreads on social media. The Formative Measurement Model for Trust served as the research model for this study, which administered questionnaires to 414 student participants. The findings indicate that that from five variables, there are three variables that have a significant effect on students' confidence in trusting the credibility of deepfake video information on social media. The variables that have a significant effect are User Knowledge, Platform, and Uploader and the variables that do not have a significant effect are Comments and Accuracy. Therefore, this study provides insight into deepfakes and students’ confidence in trusting the credibility of deepfake video information on social media. The objective is that students will become more aware of detecting deepfake videos on social media and for social media application developers to strengthen regulations and security systems to reduce the spread of deepfake videos on social media.

articleTitle: Transforming School Organization Event Management With Microsoft Power Apps and Power Automate
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: The School Events Management System (SEMS) is a comprehensive solution designed to streamline venue reservations and budget management for student organizations. This paper details SEMS's design and implementation, emphasizing its core features and technologies. SEMS integrates a unified calendar, allowing users to oversee event schedules, see venue details, and view dates efficiently. It leverages the Microsoft Power Automate AI Builder for text recognition, enabling automated reservation detail extraction and forwarding. The system also boasts a robust budget tracker, informed by financial documents like Liquidation Reports (LR), to effectively monitor and control event-related expenses. The architecture of SEMS encompasses AI model training and data processing workflows. Its deployment has markedly enhanced venue availability verification, event mapping, and budgeting operations, as well as the management of specific documents. These advancements contribute to greater transparency and cooperation among involved parties. Moreover, SEMS aids in making well-informed decisions by improving event and budget-tracking functions.

articleTitle: Comparative Web Accessibility Compliance Evaluation of the State Universities and Colleges in the Ilocos Region Philippines
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: As schools transitioned into flexible learning during the pandemic, the use of web technologies has significantly increased. School websites are used to provide timely and essential information to students, staff, and the community. However, educational institutions must consider that not all people interact with online content in the same manner, as people with disabilities may need assistive technology. This article describes a study that assessed the accessibility of the contents concerning the websites of the state universities and colleges (SUC) in the Ilocos Region in the Philippines. The assessment was conducted to verify compliance with the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.0 (WCAG 2.0) set by the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), an international standard, ISO 40500. The study primarily aims to determine if people with disabilities can access and use the websites of the SUCs based on their level of compliance with WCAG 2.0. Moreover, this study adopted the Website Accessibility Conformance Evaluation Methodology (WCAG- EM) to determine how well the website conforms to WCAG 2.0 using automated accessibility evaluation tools, TAW and WAVE. The evaluation results revealed that all the SUC websites tested did not achieve acceptable compliance with web accessibility regardless of academic prestige. By evaluating the different SUC websites of the Ilocos Region, over 700 errors have been detected mostly linked to user-interface components and information. These issues and non-compliance issues indicate a necessity to strengthen and apply better policies and directives for schools to make institutional websites more inclusive.

articleTitle: The Feasibility of Using Synthetic-Generated Dataset for Training Sentiment Analysis Model
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: New features in machine learning applications are constantly being explored demanding the availability and quality of data. To address this, the exploration of synthetic data emerges as a promising solution. This paper intends to solve the problem of data availability by finding out the feasibility of using synthetic data as a solution. Many researchers tried to use algorithms such as SMOTE and ADASYN, but encountered challenges in producing semantically and grammatically acceptable material. One of the few front-runners in synthetic text data generation is GPT 3.5. A trained sentiment analysis model would benefit users greatly by providing valuable insights into given text data, helping to understand emotions, opinions, and trends. The criteria of a high-quality dataset is providing various examples for each class. High-quality training data is crucial for accurate sentiment analysis, ensuring correct patterns, bias minimization, and reliable predictions. This paper utilizes GPT 3.5 to generate the synthetic data, with BERT and CNN-LSTM as the model architectures. Each architecture employs three models, each with a unique train-test combination that serves its own purpose. The performance of the six trained models is compared based on accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score to evaluate the quality and efficacy of synthetic data. The conducted evaluation shows that data augmentation using synthetic data is feasible. This finding is presented as the main contribution of the study. However, fully synthetic data-trained models require more refining.

articleTitle: Enhancing Engagement: Key Factors for Exceptional Learners in Gamified Education
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: This quantitative study investigates factors influencing the engagement of exceptional learners in gamified education, focusing on their demographics, engagement drivers, and challenges. A survey of 150 participants-educators, students, and administrators-was conducted across various educational settings to gather insights into these aspects and best practices for gamified learning. The study sought to answer key questions about the demographic profile of exceptional learners, factors affecting their engagement, challenges they face, and effective practices for gamified learning. Findings show that the demographic profile includes younger learners (aged 5–9 years), a majority of male participants (78%), and those with learning disabilities (65%). Key engagement drivers identified were immersive game design, rewards, and customization for students; feedback mechanisms, interactivity, and educational alignment for educators; and technical support and collaboration for administrators. Challenges reported include unclear instructions, accessibility issues, and technical problems, with students facing frequent technical difficulties and educators focusing on alignment with educational goals. The study concludes that improving feedback, interactivity, and inclusivity is crucial for enhancing gamified learning environments. Recommendations include clearer instructions, better accessibility, and robust technical support. The study highlights limitations such as potential response biases and suggests future research on how demographic factors affect perceptions of gamified learning and its long-term educational impacts.

articleTitle: Automatic Multiple Choice Question Generation: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: Despite their drawbacks, multiple-choice questions (MCQ) have been widely used to assess the students' understanding of lectures through examinations. The development of automatic MCQ generation is beneficial, especially for educators. As a starting point for further development, a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) is conducted to uncover current trends, future challenges, and opportunities in automatic MCQ generation. Previously, an SLR was conducted, but it lacks coverage of the utilization of transformer-based models. This SLR covers the development of automatic MCQ generation using either traditional or advanced approaches such as Transformers. The Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses framework was used to gather the data from Scopus, IEEE Xplore, SpringerLink, arXiv, and Semantic Scholar. The included articles must be open-access computer science conference papers or journal articles and written in English less than five years ago. Four independent reviewers analyzed the research workflow, evaluation metric, and dataset used in each study. There are 18 included studies, where 17% (n = 3) studies are from 2024, 33% (n = 6) studies are from 2023, 22% (n = 4) studies are from 2022, 11% (n = 2) studies are from 2021, and 17% (n = 3) studies are from 2020. There are 33% (n = 6) of the studies used the traditional feature-based engineering approach, 39% (n = 7) of the studies used the Transformer-based model fine-tuning approach, and the remaining used novel approaches. The study found that BERT variants are the most utilized Transformer-based model in automatic MCQ. The research notes some challenges, but also open various opportunities for further research, including Large Language Model (LLM) utilization for automatic MCQ generation, the utilization BERT-based models for standardized machine-learned evaluation metrics, and the initiative for the creation of an MCQ dataset benchmark.

articleTitle: Enhancing Emotion Recognition in Voice: Leveraging Support Vector Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: Voice analysis has emerged as a pivotal tool in emotion detection, with applications spanning customer service to aviation safety. This study investigates the effectiveness of Support Vector Machine (SVM) classification for emotion detection from voice data, focusing on the impact of feature extraction methods and dataset characteristics. Utilizing Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) for feature extraction, we evaluated SVM performance with different kernel functions and regularization parameters across two datasets: the RAVDESS and JL Corpus. The RAVDESS dataset, featuring 2,452 recordings in English, includes eight emotional categories, while the JL Corpus, with 480 recordings, encompasses ten emotions. Our results reveal that an 80% training and 20% testing split provided the highest accuracy, precision, and F1-score. The Radial Basis Function (RBF) kernel with a regularization parameter <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex> of 1000 outperformed the Linear kernel, achieving superior accuracy and faster training times. The JL Corpus dataset achieved an accuracy above 90%, while the RAVDESS dataset yielded 63% accuracy, primarily due to fluctuating amplitude patterns. Combining the datasets improved overall performance to nearly 70%, highlighting the benefits of diverse data in enhancing model generalization.

articleTitle: HyDeck: Hybrid Decider-K for IoT Intrusion Detection System
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is currently experiencing rapid growth in various sectors of human life, leading to significant advancements in technology and convenience. However, this rapid development is accompanied by security issues that pose threats to users. Traditional firewall technology falls short in identifying abnormal activities in network traffic, highlighting the necessity for an effective intrusion detection system (IDS). This research addresses this need by developing a model for intrusion detection that combines K-Means clustering, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and Decision Tree algorithms to enhance performance on imbalanced datasets. To ensure the robustness of the model, the data is divided into several folds and subjected to a thorough cross-validation process. The results indicate that the developed model achieves better accuracy for each data fold compared to a standard decision tree classifier. This improvement underscores the significant potential of hybrid models in greatly enhancing the security and reliability of IoT networks.

articleTitle: An Improved Model for People Detection Based on YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: People detection is vital for security in large-scale disaster outdoor rescue and large public spaces. Despite its success in various applications, people detection technology continues to face challenges such as low accuracy, difficulty in feature extraction, and slow model performance. This paper proposes an enhanced people detection algorithm based on You Only Look Once version 8 (YOLOv8). The algorithm introduces the Cross Stage Partial Networks with Focused Expansion and Feature Fusion Compressed Information Bottleneck (C2fCIB) module to optimize the backbone network, enhance feature extraction capabilities, and improve the detection accuracy of small and occluded targets, thereby increasing the model's overall detection accuracy. Additionally, a combined loss function incorporating Skew Intersection over Union (SIOU) and Complete Intersection over Union (CIOU) is employed to optimize the detection rate for small and occluded targets, further enhancing accuracy and expediting convergence. Experimental results demonstrate that the average detection accuracy of the improved model increased by 15.4%, and the training speed improved by 15.5%. Consequently, the enhanced model is more effective for people detection, contributing to safety in public spaces and other application scenarios. Furthermore, the model's enhancement methods offer valuable insights for researchers and experts in the field of people detection.

articleTitle: e-Filing Service Adoption: The Mediating Role of Trust in E-government Service
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: E-government services have experienced poor user acceptance and failed to meet the public's and government's expectations. Existing studies have investigated the critical success factors of e-Filing services using TAM. Unfortunately, investigations on the influence of trust in e-government are still lacking. Trust in e-government services, as a mandatory foundation of digital public service delivery, is built on digital services' perceived reliability, security, and transparency. There is still more existing knowledge that needs to be improved. This study considers trust in e-government services to enrich the existing knowledge on the critical success factors of e-Filing adoption in Indonesia. A quantitative research method was applied. Existing studies were adopted to develop the research questionnaire. An online survey link was used to distribute the questionnaire to individual taxpayers in Indonesia. The SmartPLS software was used to analyze 297 individual taxpayer respondents. The study found that perceived usefulness and trust in e-government services significantly affect actual usage, while perceived ease of use does not. The study's results prove that trust in e-government services plays an essential mediating role in perceived usefulness and ease of use in adopting e-government services. The causal relationship between perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use to actual e-government usage is also presented. Thus, trust in e-government services needs to be a special consideration for policymakers and developers of digital service systems in the future. Future research can also consider other factors in the proposed model for more in-depth analysis.

articleTitle: Parameter Efficient Fine-tuning using Low-Rank Adaptation for Emotion Classification in Indonesian Texts
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: The rapid expansion of social media has created a dynamic platform in which individuals regularly share their thoughts and emotions, leading to the generation of extensive textual data. This vast amount of data offers both an opportunity and a challenge for automatic emotion recognition, as effective utilization requires advanced models capable of accurately classifying emotions across varied linguistic contexts. In this study, we conducted a comparative analysis of emotion classification using Transformer models, specifically IndoBERTweet, Multilingual BERT, and XLM-RoBERTa, with a focus on full-parameter fine-tuning and Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA). The experiments demonstrated that although PEFT with LoRA significantly reduces the number of trainable parameters, it can still achieve competitive performance compared to full-parameter fine-tuning, with XLM-RoBERTa (large) showing the highest precision, recall, and Macro-F1 score. However, the underperformance of M-BERT when using PEFT highlights the complexity of optimizing these models, indicating that not all models are equally suited to this fine-tuning approach. These findings suggest that PEFT methods such as LoRA can be effective alternatives to full-parameter fine-tuning, particularly for larger models. Future research could compare Transformer models across different languages and emotion classification tasks, explore alternative PEFT methods beyond LoRA, investigate the effects of LoRA on different Transformer layers, and examine hybrid fine-tuning approaches for improved efficiency and performance, especially for models such as M-BERT.

articleTitle: The Role of AI Chatbots on E-Commerce Platforms: Understanding its Influence on Customer Trust and Dependability
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: This study investigates the role of AI chatbots in enhancing customer trust and dependability on e-commerce platforms. With the changing landscape of business due to advancements AI chatbots have become crucial tools for customer engagement and simplifying transactions. The study explores factors that affect customer trust, such as chatbot knowledge, humanlike qualities, responsiveness and brand reputation. By collecting data from 209 e-commerce users in Indonesia through a survey using quantitative methods the study discovered that expertise and responsiveness play a significant role in enhancing trust in AI chatbots leading to increased reliance by customers on these systems. Surprisingly, brand reputation alone did not have a direct effect on chatbot trust. The research emphasizes the need to optimize chatbot features to build user trust and suggests that while humanlike characteristics can improve interactions the main focus should be on efficiency. These findings provide insights for businesses looking to use AI chatbots effectively to enhance customer satisfaction and loyalty in today's competitive e-commerce environment.

articleTitle: Investigating Intention to Use Digital Securities Crowdfunding Platforms: Insights from TAM and UTAUT Frameworks
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: This study considers and analyzes the components impacting the intention to use Digital Securities Crowdfunding Platforms among Indonesian investors centering on factors influencing their usage intention. The inquiry about coordinating the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) to analyze the effect of perceived ease of use, perceived benefits, perceived usefulness, social influence, trust, perceived risk, and intention to use. A test of 403 respondents from the Jabodetabek region, as a representative of Indonesia's populace, was overviewed. The information examination was performed utilizing Structural Equation Modeling-Partial Least Squares (SEMPLS). Several measurements, such as Cronbach's Alpha, rho_A, Composite Reliability (CR), and Average Variance Extracted (AVE), are used to assess the viability and reliability of the measurement model. The discoveries uncover critical relationships between perceived risk, intention to use, perceived usefulness, social influence, and trust. The results emphasize the significance of these components in forming investors' decisions to embrace digital securities crowdfunding platforms. By highlighting the roles of social influence, perceived usefulness, and trust, this research enhances our understanding of investor behavior in the context of digital securities crowdfunding. The insights provided by this study can inform platform developers and policymakers aiming to increase adoption rates and improve the overall effectiveness of digital securities crowdfunding initiatives in Indonesia.

articleTitle: Opinion Mining of Gojek User Satisfaction from Social Media Platform X Using SVM Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: Transportation is a necessary component of human life. In recent years, social media has become a significant platform for expressing opinions, aspirations, criticism, and suggestions to the general public through text, videos, and images. Users can freely provide input and express opinions. One of the most popular social media applications for expressing opinions is Twitter, which rebranded to X in 2023. Users can discuss a wide range of topics including sports, entertainment, technology, culinary arts, politics, and social issues that are currently viral or trending. A particularly popular topic among X users is the review of various products, places, services, and experiences. Among the frequently discussed services are transportation services. One of the most widely used means of transportation today is online motorcycle taxis, with Gojek being the leading application in Indonesia. This paper aims to analyze the sentiment level of satisfaction among users of online motorcycle taxi services, specifically Gojek, by collecting user reviews from the social media platform and conducting tweet sentiment analysis.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Agricultural Marketing in Ilocos Norte: A Location-Based Platform for Connecting Small Scale Farmers and Consumers
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to develop technological innovation and solution, specifically a location-based platform utilizing Geographic Information System (GIS) that connects small-scale farmers, consumers and wholesalers. The study directly benefits smallholder farmers and wholesalers in Ilocos Norte, Philippines, by providing farmers and wholesalers with the necessary technology to generate income through direct sales of their agricultural products to potential buyers specifically wholesalers. By bypassing intermediaries and middlemen, farmers can potentially achieve higher profits, while prospective wholesalers, including those purchasing in bulk, can enjoy lower prices, on agricultural products. The direct connection between farmers and wholesalers through this online platform addresses weaknesses in the existing trading system and creates a more equitable and efficient market environment for smallholder farmers and wholesalers. The study is focused on developing a location-based marketplace system that directly connects smallholder farmers in Ilocos Norte to wholesalers, eliminating the need for middlemen in the process.

articleTitle: Identification and Authentication System of User Voice in Bahasa Indonesia using MFCC and Support Vector Classifier
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: Over the last decade, deep learning techniques have gained significant attention and are widely adopted across various domains, such as speech recognition and computer vision. This widespread integration is primarily due to the increased availability of extensive datasets, advancements in hardware performance, and continuous improvements in deep learning software and algorithms. These developments have paved the way for applying deep learning techniques to voice recognition. The remarkable ability of deep learning models to learn complex representations from large datasets enables them to recognize individual voices, often surpassing traditional statistical methods accurately. Nevertheless, implementing voice recognition systems for Bahasa Indonesia has faced difficulties due to the language's distinctive linguistic features. The lack of diverse and representative datasets for Bahasa Indonesia is an area that requires further attention and investment. This research aims to present a novel deep learning-based method for voice recognition, explicitly focusing on the challenges and opportunities within the context of the Bahasa Indonesia language. The paper proposes a robust and accurate voice recognition system for Bahasa Indonesia speakers, leveraging Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients for feature extraction from voice data and a Support Vector Classifier for classification. The accuracy of the data speaker recognition reached 90% for the polynomial kernel and 83.33% for the linear kernel.

articleTitle: Exploring the Landscape of Tourism Knowledge Graphs: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: Knowledge graphs (KGs) are important tools for organizing and leveraging machine-readable knowledge across various domains. This paper presents a systematic literature review examining the state of research on tourism knowledge graphs (TKGs). Our review followed Kitchenham guidelines and developed four research questions to accomplish the objectives of the study. We analyzed 35 relevant studies from 151 English-language publications published between 2013 and 2023 to identify trends in TKG construction, application, and evaluation. Our findings revealed that TKGs are predominantly built using graph data models such as RDF and LPG, stored in graph databases such as GraphDB and Neo4J, and extracted from diverse tourism data sources. The main applications include tourism recommender systems, question-answering systems, conversational assistants, and data analytics. European TKG projects prioritize semantic interoperability, while Asian projects focus on performance optimization. The TKG quality is evaluated primarily through metrics of correctness and completeness or through case study applications. However, our review identified several key gaps: limited scope of applications focusing primarily on tourist-centric use cases, lack of comprehensive construction methodologies, insufficient evaluation across multiple quality dimensions, and underutilization of TKGs for sustainable and responsible tourism practices. We propose directions for future research to address these limitations, including developing TKGs to support sustainable tourism practices, integrating TKGs with emerging technologies, expanding applications to benefit a wider range of stakeholders, and enhancing evaluation methodologies. This study contributes to the advancement of intelligent tourism systems by providing a comprehensive overview of the TKG landscape and guiding future research efforts.

articleTitle: Improving Intrusion Detection System on Servers using Machine Learning-Based RFERF Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) are essential for network security, but they also come with several critical security issues that can affect their effectiveness and reliability. One of the critical issues in IDS is the emergence of false positives in detection results. An IDS might incorrectly identify legitimate activities as malicious, leading to unnecessary alerts. It can overwhelm security teams with false alarms, causing alert fatigue and potentially causing real threats to be overlooked. In addition, IDS performance does not achieve maximum accuracy in detecting attacks. Therefore, to address this problem, this research proposes a machine learning-based system security model called RFERF (Recursive Feature Elimination with Random Forest). This model was built with two levels of technical approaches simultaneously: a strategy at the data level and an approach at the algorithm level. At the data level, RFE-based feature selection techniques are applied to obtain the best subset of the dataset. Meanwhile, the approach at the algorithm level applies the Random Forest (RF) algorithm as a classifier in the detector engine. Then, the proposed model is tested and validated using the CIC-IDS2017 dataset. The model's performance is evaluated through a confusion matrix by calculating the accuracy, recall, precision, f1-score, kappa score values, and testing time. The experimental results show that the proposed model (RFERF) can outperform other models. The accuracy obtained is 99.95%. However, a limitation of this model is its slower speed compared to the Random Forest (RF) model, which operates at 613ms, while RFERF takes 1.190ms. In future research, we aim to enhance the model's performance to optimize its speed. Process speed has implications for IDS performance in detecting attacks.

articleTitle: Confidentiality. Integrity, and Availability (CIA) Approach for Private Dataset Management System Design
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: Dataset management systems are essential for assisting research and development (R&D) organizations in applying data governance protocols, especially in managing the utilization of datasets. In R&D, datasets are vital sources for producing analysis, machine learning prediction, and supporting decision-making. As such, it is important to deploy dataset management systems with considerations regarding the aspects of Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability (CIA) which is a design principle that emphasized information protection and collaboration facilitation among dataset users. The study proposed an analysis and a design for a dataset management system that takes CIA aspects into account. In the future, the proposed design will be utilized as a benchmark for building a dataset management system. In this study, the Waterfall method was adopted. A use case diagram, an ERD (Entity Relationship Diagram), and an activity diagram were constructed in the design stage. In the project implementation stage, the Laravel framework including Laravel Jetstream was considered to be used.

articleTitle: Large Language Model: Design Mobile Platform for Problem Solving Ideation
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Information Technology and Digital Applications (ICITDA)
abstract: This study focuses on creating a platform design using the TRIZ method to solve problems in business and management. TRIZ is known for its structured approach to problem-solving and has been effective in promoting innovation and improvement in products, services, and systems. However, while TRIZ is generally user-friendly, it is challenging to learn and apply it well. This often requires the help of TRIZ experts working with people who understand the specific area to find the best solutions. Since it was first developed, TRIZ has become much more important in business and management, helping with key areas like human resources and how organizations work. TRIZ remains vital in improving how problems are solved by serving different types of organizations, including social enterprises and non-profits. To overcome the challenges of using TRIZ, IT-based platforms have been very helpful, but the guidance of TRIZ experts is still crucial. Additionally, the rise of artificial intelligence (AI), especially Generative AI models, offers an exciting way to enhance TRIZ methods. Generative AI allows algorithms to analyze various data sources and create content such as text, images, audio, and video. Using Generative AI, interactions between users and systems become more human-like, allowing users to explain the specifics of their problems and what they want to achieve. AI then provides solutions based on TRIZ principles. The method used in this study includes Function Analysis (FA) modeling, which has three main stages: component analysis, interaction analysis, and function modeling. The result of this study is a user-friendly Generative AI function design, shown as a prompt interface that works with TRIZ knowledge. This interface provides users solution suggestions that match their goals, thus making the problem-solving process in business and management easier.
